title: High-Protein Paneer Bhurji
description: Scrambled cottage cheese tossed with onion, ripe tomatoes, fresh green chillies, and aromatic spices.

ingredients.note: crumbled fresh low-fat or standard paneer

steps: Heat 10g desi cow ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan on medium heat.
Add finely chopped onions and sauté for 4-5 minutes until golden and translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, cumin powder, red chilli powder, and salt. Cook until tomatoes turn mushy.
Crumble 250g fresh paneer and gently fold it into the spiced onion-tomato masala.
Sauté for 3-4 minutes on low flame to retain softness without releasing moisture. Garnish with chopped fresh coriander leaves.
tips: Do not overcook paneer beyond 4 minutes to avoid rubberiness.
Serve warm with whole wheat phulkas or toasted sourdough.

title: High-Protein Soya Chunks Curry
description: Juicy textured soya nuggets simmered in a homestyle onion-tomato gravy with warm garam masala.
steps: Boil 100g dry soya chunks in lightly salted water for 5 minutes until soft and doubled in size.
Rinse under cold water and squeeze thoroughly to eliminate any bitterness.
Heat 10g olive oil in a pan, add chopped onions, and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and chopped tomatoes; cook until the masala leaves oil on the edges.
Add the squeezed soya chunks and 1 cup of warm water. Simmer covered for 8-10 minutes.
Finish with freshly ground garam masala and fresh cilantro.
tips: Squeezing out the water thoroughly is key to absorbing the aromatic curry flavors.

title: Homestyle Yellow Dal Tadka
description: Comforting yellow moong lentils tempered with cumin, garlic, and golden desi cow ghee.
steps: Rinse yellow moong dal and pressure cook with 3 cups water, turmeric, and salt for 3 whistles.
In a tadka pan, heat 10g desi cow ghee, add cumin seeds, and let them crackle.
Add chopped onions and fry until light brown, then add chopped tomatoes until soft.
Pour the sizzling tadka directly over the cooked dal and stir well.
Simmer for 2 minutes and garnish with fresh coriander.
tips: For a vegan version, substitute ghee with mustard oil or olive oil.

title: Savory Masala Oats with Boiled Eggs
description: Nutritious rolled oats infused with Indian spices and sautéed vegetables, topped with protein-packed boiled eggs.
steps: Heat 5g ghee in a pan and lightly sauté chopped onions and tomatoes.
Add 80g rolled oats along with turmeric, cumin, and black pepper; roast for 1 minute.
Pour in 2 cups of water and salt, bringing to a gentle boil on medium heat.
Cook for 4-5 minutes stirring occasionally until thick and creamy.
Halve 2 large boiled eggs and arrange neatly on top before serving.
tips: Toss in green peas, diced carrots, or baby spinach for extra micronutrients.

title: Tandoori Spiced Grilled Chicken Breast
description: Lean chicken breast marinated in thick curd, Kashmiri red chilli, kasuri methi, and grilled to tender perfection.
steps: Score chicken breasts lightly with shallow diagonal cuts for deep marinade penetration.
In a bowl, mix 60g curd, Kashmiri chilli powder, garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, and salt.
Coat chicken thoroughly and let marinate for at least 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Brush a cast-iron skillet or grill pan with 10g olive oil on medium-high heat.
Grill chicken for 6-7 minutes per side until the internal temperature reaches 74°C (165°F).
Rest for 5 minutes before slicing, then serve with lemon wedges and mint chutney.
tips: Resting the chicken after cooking locks in juices so it never dries out.
